newsitem.title: PERU: Rebel spokesman rejects talks outdside residence.
newsitem.headline: Rebel spokesman rejects talks outdside residence.

text.p: The international spokesman for the Marxist group holding 73 hostages in the Japanese ambassador's home denied on Saturday the rebels would meet with government negotiators outside the residence.

"A meeting has to be within the residence," Isaac Velazco told Reuters by telephone from Copenhagen, adding neither the Red Cross nor the Canadian government, whom the government announced would attend such talks, "can guarantee the physical safety of the commander," rebel leader Nestor Cerpa Cartolini.

Government negotiator Education Minister Domingo Palermo told a news conference on Friday arrangements had been made for him to meet Cerpa in a building near the besieged residence for talks aimed at solving the month-old crisis.

Although Palermo presented the meeting as definite -- adding that a Red Cross vehicle would transport Cerpa to the site -- it was not clear if the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) had agreed to it.

"I think the government -- with its speculative statements -- is trying to spoil the negotiation process," Velazco said. He added the MRTA's "global proposal" was negotiable, but that the rebels would not dicuss any specific demand separately. The MRTA's main demand is for the government to free some 400 jailed comrades, but they also want better prison conditions and a revamping of the judicial system for rebels.
The MRTA, who have freed about 550 hostages, still hold 73 captives, including two Peruvian ministers, the Japanese and Bolivian ambassadors and about two dozen Japanese businessmen.
